extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting health-related preprints to medRxiv
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and screening criteria for posting unpublished manuscripts describing human health research on the medRxiv preprint server, including scope, ethical and identifying-information requirements, file formats, licensing, revision/withdrawal rules, and commenting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrefereed preprint notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles on medRxiv have not been finalized by authors, might contain errors, and report information that has not yet been accepted or endorsed in any way by the scientific or medical community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and journalists should consider this when discussing medRxiv work and emphasize it has yet to be evaluated by the medical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: medRxiv posting is not peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to medRxiv are not certified by scientific peer review, edited, or typeset before being posted online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some manuscripts may be undergoing peer review and journals or other organizations may post peer reviews alongside preprints in the article dashboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility for content
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are solely responsible for the content posted on medRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv only screens for appropriateness; authors remain accountable for accuracy and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening criteria on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are screened on submission for plagiarism, non-scientific content, inappropriate article types, and material that could potentially endanger the health of individual patients or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening also checks for ethical oversight, clinical trial registration, and information that might identify a patient/participant. Screening typically completes within 2–4 days but may take longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission fee
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fee to submit manuscripts to medRxiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing relative to journal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can be submitted to medRxiv at any time up to the point it is published by a journal; if a manuscript has been published by a journal, it cannot be submitted to medRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript is already published in a journal it is ineligible for posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct submission to journals (M2J/J2M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can directly submit from medRxiv to an increasing number of journals; options appear in the Author Area after submission/revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current list of integrated journals is available on medRxiv About and Submit pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check journal policies on preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals will consider manuscripts previously posted as preprints; authors should consult lists (e.g., Wikipedia, SHERPA/RoMEO) and individual journal websites or contact the journal if in doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv provides information on which journals accept direct submission or cosubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — acceptable content (in scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv is for complete but unpublished manuscripts that describe human health research conducted, analyzed, and interpreted according to scientific principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-scope types: research articles with new data; research design protocols; data articles; systematic and scoping reviews with meta-analyses; bibliometric studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — unacceptable content (out of scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv is NOT intended for: case reports or case series; work not premised on modern biology/physiology/allopathic medicine; preclinical work; veterinary studies; narrative reviews; editorials/letters/opinion pieces; announcements of tools or services; rebuttals; addenda; hypotheses without new data; laboratory protocols/recipes; meeting reports; guidelines; policy statements or analyses; theses/undergraduate dissertations; individual components of research articles (figures/tables/datasets); protocols for systematic reviews as standalone items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles of these types will be considered out of scope and will not be posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to bioRxiv when out of medRxiv scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is better suited for bioRxiv during screening, medRxiv will notify the author and close the medRxiv submission; the transfer process ensures screening by the appropriate team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bioRxiv and medRxiv have separate scope and screening procedures; both are indexed similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject category assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must assign their preprint to one of ~50 subject categories when posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories are used for feeds and posts; this is not a formal ontology and only one subject area may be selected to avoid redundant feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial/interventional study posting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocols or results of clinical trials and other prospective interventional studies can be posted provided they are formatted as a traditional scientific paper, include a trial ID from an ICMJE-recognized registry, and have approval from an appropriate ethics oversight body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For novel drugs/devices an exemption from trial registration is permitted only if registered for emergency use by an appropriate national/international body (e.g., IND/IDE by US FDA). medRxiv requires registration of all prospective interventional studies; if not registered, authors will be asked to retrospectively register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of clinical trial
rubrics_metrics.description: A clinical trial is any research project that prospectively assigns a person or group to an intervention to study the relationship between a health-related intervention and a health-related outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions include drugs, surgical procedures, devices, behavioral treatments, educational programs, dietary interventions, quality improvement interventions, and process-of-care changes; outcomes include educational, behavioral, cognitive, biological, pharmacokinetic measures, and adverse events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal language caution
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv strongly recommends that authors avoid using causal language unless justified by a robust causal inference framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers with inappropriate causal language may be declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews that include reproducible methodology and meta-analyses may be appropriate for medRxiv; narrative reviews, viewpoints and essays that primarily summarize existing knowledge are not appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PRISMA guidelines is recommended for systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods/protocols posting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete health-related research articles summarizing new experimental or computational methods and tools are appropriate and may include step-by-step protocols; tool announcements and step-by-step protocols alone are not sufficient and must be placed in the context of a complete research article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical research design protocols presented as a complete article may be posted; standalone protocols for systematic/scoping reviews should be supplemental files rather than main submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational and disease-modeling papers criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational/mathematical papers and disease modeling papers are welcome but should be full research papers that include methodological details and results and address a research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple automated analyses of public data, facile database searches, straightforward correlations/extrapolations, or resource/tool announcements without detailed methods and research data are generally insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: No case reports/case series
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical case reports and case series may not be posted on medRxiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: No images or information that could identify individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv does not post articles that include images or information that could identify an individual; obscuring, blurring, covering, or pixelation of faces is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should remove all figure elements containing photographs where an individual's face or other identifying features are present prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying information — direct identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct identifiers that must be removed include real names or initials, official document numbers, patient/sample IDs, photographs of people, biometric data, identifying marks or text on images of body parts, precise ages (as opposed to age ranges), specific family relationships, exact dates/times and geographic locations linked to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information should be removed before posting; medRxiv will ask authors to remove identifying information before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying information — indirect identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect identifiers (fewer than three together) include age ranges, ethnicity, religion, family details and medical history, occupation, and handwriting samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If combinations of indirect identifiers could identify patients, authors should remove them and advise readers to contact the authors to request access; content that cannot be removed and is potentially sensitive should be submitted to a journal for peer review instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses/rebuttals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv is not intended for commentary that simply contests or rebuts research published in journals; manuscripts that augment or challenge earlier work with bona fide new data and/or complete re-analyses of published datasets may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must be submitted in English as medRxiv can only screen English content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors wish to make material in another language available they should advise readers to contact the corresponding author or provide a link elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and licensing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain copyright and can choose among distribution/reuse options ranging from No reuse/adaptation without permission to CC0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses supported include: No reuse/adaptation without permission; CC-BY-NC-ND; CC-BY-ND; CC-BY-NC; CC-BY; CC0. License selection determines reuse parameters and is displayed on the manuscript page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright infringement / DMCA process
rubrics_metrics.description: openRxiv will respond to notices of alleged copyright infringement that comply with applicable law and the DMCA; notices must include specified elements (signature, identification of work, location of material, contact info, statements of good faith and accuracy, and authorization to act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designated copyright agent and address are provided; failure to comply with DMCA requirements may render notices ineffective; repeat infringers may have accounts disabled/terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for content they submit, including material produced by generative AI and related technologies; use of these tools should be detailed in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI output must not plagiarize or breach copyright; authors are accountable for accuracy and originality. AI tools and LLMs do not meet authorship criteria and should not be listed as authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-server posting recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv strongly recommends that a preprint be posted on only one server; posting to more than one server (e.g., both medRxiv and bioRxiv) is not permitted and will result in withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv provides article metrics and posting on multiple servers underestimates those metrics and creates confusion in citations; manuscripts already on other servers will not be posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit a single PDF or individual text and figure files; acceptable text formats: Word, WordPerfect, PDF; TeX/LaTeX must be converted to PDF; acceptable image formats: GIF, TIFF, EPS, JPEG and common word-processing table formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid images with transparent backgrounds as they will not display correctly. Supplemental files are posted 'as is' and must be accessible to medRxiv screeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posted formats and conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints are posted first as PDF (author-created) and then converted to full text HTML and XML; full text HTML typically posts 1–2 days after the PDF; XML is available for text mining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A print-friendly version with in-line figures is generated from the full text HTML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata extraction and changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata (title, author list, abstract) initially post as supplied by the author but are replaced with final metadata extracted from the PDF once full text HTML is generated; small differences may occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid submitting revisions solely to fix metadata errors that are correct in the PDF because those will be updated automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision policy and substantial updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions are intended for substantially updating manuscript content (new datasets, reanalyses, expanded discussion or supplemental information). A manuscript posted on medRxiv can be revised at any time until it is published in a journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit a revision, use the 'Submit a revision' link in the Author Area; revised versions post under the same DOI and the original remains accessible in the Info/History tab. If the content has changed sufficiently to be a different article, submit as a new manuscript for a new DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision process for J2M (journal-to-medRxiv) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: To revise a paper that was submitted to medRxiv indirectly via a journal (J2M), the corresponding author must register at medRxiv with the same email used during journal submission and then submit revisions through the medRxiv submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silent name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv allows author name changes defined as an update to an individual's first/last name without an accompanying revision or correction notice (a 'silent' change) if an author requests this; no explanation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not cover author removals or author list re-ordering. Non-silent name changes can be made by submitting a revised version of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental files revision requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have changes to Supplemental files but not to the previously posted preprint main text, you must resubmit the main article with the revised Supplemental files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal vs removal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts posted to medRxiv receive DOIs and are citable and part of the scientific record; they cannot be removed. Authors may withdraw a manuscript and post a withdrawal statement; the original manuscript remains accessible and a 'Withdrawn' watermark is added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To withdraw, use 'Submit a Withdrawal Statement' in the Author Area. In extremely rare cases, papers have been removed for legal or safety reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical oversight requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of ethical oversight by an independent dedicated oversight body (e.g., Ethics Committee, Institutional Review Board) is required for all cases in which human subjects, samples or data were used for research purposes, unless the data are already openly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv does NOT accept decisions from online tools, audit bodies, Caldicott Guardians, biosafety/data-handling committees, Human Resources, or Research & Development Departments. Ethical oversight must cover the entire study and all human samples, data, and patient cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv preprints are indexed by major search engines and services (Google, Google Scholar, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC, Preprint Citation Index), and NIH-funded preprints are indexed by PubMed; all medRxiv papers are archived at Portico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints should be cited using their DOI; if citing a specific version, add the version-specific URL or version number (e.g., 'version 2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided in the FAQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH application citation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH encourages investigators to use interim research products, such as preprints, in applications and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv preprints may be cited in NIH applications per NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channels (curated collections) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels are curated collections of preprints that share the subject focus of an organization; medRxiv does not curate algorithmically and a curator from the organization is required to manually tag appropriate papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations interested in maintaining a Channel should contact medRxiv staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area alerts subscription
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can subscribe to Subject Area Alerts by checking subject categories on the Sign Up for Subject Area Alerts page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscriptions can be added or removed at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics provided for preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv provides metrics for all preprints, including Abstract and PDF views updated daily and Altmetric attention scores (blogs, tweets, news, other media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics are available in each preprint's Metrics tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting policy and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can be submitted via Disqus on each preprint version and should address the scientific content, including feedback and specific questions about methodology, results, or data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprint reviews may be submitted as comments but must not include journal, reviewer, or editor names. Comments must be in English, submitted only once, are moderated (24–48 h), and any comments not directly related to content, violating policy, offensive, or questioning authors' character will be excluded. medRxiv cannot correspond with commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulk access and API availability
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv provides free and unrestricted access to all articles; a variety of resources, APIs and feeds support machine analysis and bulk access to full text and metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk mitigation and prominent disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv mitigates risk by screening for non-scientific content, lack of ethical oversight or trial registration, excessive identifying information, or content that could endanger the public, and all preprints are accompanied by a prominent statement that they have not been certified by peer review and should not be used to directly inform clinical decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDFs also receive a stamp indicating lack of peer review.
